h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר י׳ Pesach — Maamar Yud

p: בַּפִּיּוּט לְמוּסַף טַל נִתְקַן עַל דֶּרֶךְ תַּשְׁרַ"ק:
In the piyut for the Musaf prayer of Tal (Dew), it was composed in reverse alphabetical order (tashrak):
תֵּן לִרְצוֹת וְכוּלֵּי;
"Grant favor, etc.";
וּבְפִיּוּט גֶּשֶׁם עַל דֶּרֶךְ אָלֶ"ף בֵּי"ת:
whereas in the piyut of Geshem (Rain), it was composed in standard alphabetical order (alef-beis):
זְכוֹר אָב וְכוּלֵּי.
"Remember the patriarch, etc."
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
And in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' קפ"ו.)
אִיתָא:
it is stated:
יַרְחָא דִּלְכוֹן אִיהוּ כְּסִדְרָן דְּאַתְוָון: אָבִי"ב
"Your month (Nisan) follows the standard order of the letters: Aviv
דְּאִיהוּ י"ב, רָזָא דְּג'
which equals twelve, the secret of three
(הַיְינוּ בְּמִסְפָּר קָטָן י"ב — ג'),
(that is, in reduced numerology, twelve reduces to three)
אב"ג כְּסִדְרָא דְּאַתְוָון;
Alef-Beis-Gimmel, in the forward order of the letters;
אֲבָל יַרְחָא שְׁבִיעָאָה דִּילִי מִסּוֹפָא דְּאַתְוָון: תש"ר
whereas My seventh month (Tishrei) proceeds from the end of the letters: Tashrei (Tav-Shin-Reish).
מַאי טַעְמָא?
What is the reason?
אַתּוּן מִתַּתָּא לְעֵילָּא וַאֲנָא מֵעֵילָּא לְתַתָּא.
You ascend from below to above, while I descend from above to below."
וְהַיְינוּ אָלֶ"ף בֵּי"ת מִתַּתָּא לְעֵילָּא, תַּשְׁרַ"ק מֵעֵילָּא לְתַתָּא.
That is, alef-beis goes from below to above, while tashrak goes from above to below.
וְכֵן הָאֲרִי הַקָּדוֹשׁ חָשַׁב שִׁשָּׁה חָדְשֵׁי הַקַּיִץ דְּמַטְרוֹנִיתָא, שִׁשָּׁה חָדְשֵׁי הַחֹרֶף דְּמַלְכָּא.

And similarly, the holy Arizal reckoned the six months of summer as belonging to the Queen (Matronisa, Knesses Yisrael) and the six months of winter as belonging to the King (Malka, the Holy One, blessed is He).
וְלָמָּה בַּעֲלֵי הַפִּיּוּט סִידְּרוּ לְהֵיפֶךְ:
Why, then, did the composers of the piyutim arrange them in the reverse:
שֶׁהַתְּפִלָּה עַל טַל הוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ תַּשְׁרַ"ק
so that the prayer for Tal (recited in Nisan, summer) follows tashrak,
וְעַל גֶּשֶׁם דֶּרֶךְ אָלֶ"ף בֵּי"ת?
while the prayer for Geshem (recited in Tishrei, winter) follows alef-beis?
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן: שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי תִּשְׁרֵי הִיא כְּפִי שֶׁעָלָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה לִבְרוֹא הָעוֹלָם,
However, the explanation is that certainly Tishrei corresponds to how it initially arose in Divine thought to create the world,
וְהָיָה לְהוֹרִיד הַשְּׁכִינָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה עִיקָּר בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים:
which was to bring the Divine Presence down so that Its primary dwelling would be in the lower realms:
תש"ר מֵעֵילָּא לְתַתָּא.
Tav-Shin-Reish, from above to below.
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי מַזְכִּירִין שָׁם הָאָבוֹת וּמֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן שֶׁהֵם הוֹרִידוּ הַשְּׁכִינָה לְמַטָּה
And for this reason, we mention there (in the Geshem prayer) the Patriarchs, Moshe, and Aharon, who drew the Divine Presence downward
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה י"ט, ז').
(Bereishis Rabbah 19:7).
וּבְנִיסָן שֶׁנִּבְרָא הָעוֹלָם
Whereas in Nisan, when the world was actually created
(וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כ"ז. דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל כְּמַאן בְּמַחֲלוֹקֶת דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ דְּאֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים),
(and as Tosafos wrote in Rosh Hashanah 27a, s.v. K'man, regarding the dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua, that "both these and those are the words of the living God"),
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁצָּפָה שֶׁאֵין הָעוֹלָם מִתְקַיֵּים,
that reflects how He foresaw that the world could not endure [under strict judgment alone],
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיְּקַלְקְלוּ, וְצָרִיךְ הָאָדָם לְבָרֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ עַל יְדֵי עֲבוֹדָתוֹ,
meaning that humanity would sin, and man must refine himself through his own spiritual service
וְזֶה מִתַּתָּא לְעֵילָּא וְאַתְוָון כְּסִדְרָן אב"ג, וְהֵם חָדְשֵׁי דְּמַטְרוֹנִיתָא.
and this is from below to above, with the letters in their standard order, Alef-Beis-Gimmel, which are the months of the Queen.
וְכֵן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ נִמְשָׁל לְגֶשֶׁם,
And similarly, the Written Torah, which comes from the side of Hashem, may He be blessed, is compared to rain,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
as it is said
(דְּבָרִים ל"ב, ב'):
(Devarim 32:2):
יַעֲרֹף כַּמָּטָר לִקְחִי,
"May my teaching drop like the rain"
וְהַיְינוּ לֶקַח טוֹב, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב.
which refers to "a goodly teaching," the Written Torah.
וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל נִמְשָׁל לְטַל,
And the Oral Torah, which comes from the side of Knesses Yisrael, is compared to dew,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
as it is said
(ibid.):
תִּזַּל כַּטַּל אִמְרָתִי.
"May my utterance distill like the dew."
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ, שֶׁכְּמוֹ הַטַּל אֵינוֹ נִיכָּר שֶׁהוּא מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם,
And as we have explained, just as dew is not visibly seen descending from the heavens,
רַק מִמַּה שֶּׁרוֹאִין שֶׁהָאָרֶץ לַחָה יוֹדְעִין שֶׁיָּרַד הַטַּל,
and only from seeing that the earth is moist do people know that dew has fallen,
כֵּן הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים שֶׁנּוֹזֵל מֵה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלֵב חֲכָמִים,
so too is the Oral Torah—the words of the living God that flow from Hashem, may He be blessed, into the hearts of the Sages,
וְאֵינוֹ נִיכָּר, שֶׁנִּרְאֶה שֶׁהֵם מְחַדְּשִׁים מִשִּׂכְלָם.
yet it is not overtly apparent, for it appears as though they are innovating from their own intellect.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: תִּזַּל כַּטַּל אִמְרָתִי,
And this is what is meant by "May my utterance distill like the dew"
וְהַיְינוּ אֲמִירָה בַּחֲשַׁאי, כְּמָה דְּאַתְּ אָמַר
which is a whispered utterance, as it is said
(יְשַׁעְיָה מ"ט, כ"א):
(Yeshayahu 49:21):
וְאָמַרְתְּ בִּלְבָבֵךְ
"And you shall say in your heart"
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק א' רל"ד:),
(Zohar, Vol. 1, 234b),
שֶׁמּוֹפִיעַ ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלֵב הַחֲכָמִים.
meaning that Hashem, may He be blessed, shines into the hearts of the Sages.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הַגֶּשֶׁם בָּא עַל יְדֵי מַעֲשֵׂה הַצַּדִּיקִים,
Nevertheless, rain comes through the deeds of the righteous,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
as they said
(כְּתוּבּוֹת ה'.):
(Kesubos 5a):
מַעֲשֵׂה יְדֵיהֶם שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים מִי מַגִּיד? הָרָקִיעַ; וּמַאי נִיהוּ? מָטָר.
"Who declares the handiwork of the righteous? The firmament; and what is it? Rain."
וְכֵן מָצִינוּ
And so we find
(מוֹעֵד קָטָן כ"ח.):
(Moed Katan 28a):
דְּהָא רַבָּה וְרַב חִסְדָּא תַּרְוַיְיהוּ רַבָּנָן צַדִּיקֵי הֲווֹ,
"Behold, Rabbah and Rav Chisda were both righteous rabbis:
מָר מְצַלֵּי וְאָתֵי מִיטְרָא, וּמָר מְצַלֵּי וְאָתֵי מִיטְרָא וְכוּלֵּי
one prayed and rain came, and the other prayed and rain came, etc."
שֶׁבָּזֶה נִיכָּר שֶׁהֵם צַדִּיקִים שֶׁמִּתְפַּלְּלִין עַל הַגֶּשֶׁם וּבָא;
for through this it is recognized that they are righteous, that they pray for rain and it comes;
וְכֵן
and likewise
(תַּעֲנִית ט':):
(Taanis 9b):
מָטָר בִּשְׁבִיל יָחִיד וְכוּלֵּי, הַאי מֵישְׁרָא בָּעְיָא מַיָּא וְהַאי מֵישְׁרָא לָא בָּעְיָא מַיָּא וְאָתָא מִיטְרָא וְכוּלֵּי
"Rain falls for the sake of a single individual, etc.; this valley needed water and that valley did not need water, and rain came, etc."
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַטַּל דְּלָא מִיעְצַר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם
unlike dew, which is never withheld, as they said there
(Taanis 3a),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁתָּמִיד מַשְׁפִּיעַ ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ הַטַּל.
meaning that Hashem, may He be blessed, constantly bestows dew.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם נִמְשָׁל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב לְגֶשֶׁם: יַעֲרֹף כַּמָּטָר לִקְחִי,
Still, the Written Torah is compared to rain—"May my teaching drop like the rain"
שֶׁאַחַר שֶׁזּוֹכִין לְהַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב נִיכָּר הוּא שֶׁהוּא מֵה' יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּמוֹ הַמָּטָר,
because once one merits the Written Torah, it is overtly recognizable that it comes from Hashem, may He be blessed, just like rain,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
as it is said
(Mishlei 2:6):
כִּי ה' יִתֵּן חָכְמָה וְגוֹמֵר;
"For Hashem gives wisdom, etc."
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁנִּדְמֶה לַחֲכָמִים שֶׁהֵם מְחַדְּשִׁים מִלִּבָּם, וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי נִמְשָׁל כַּטַּל וְכָאָמוּר.
unlike the Oral Torah, which appears to the Sages as though they are innovating from their own minds, and for that reason is compared to dew, as stated.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַטַּל מֵה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁמַּשְׁפִּיעַ תָּמִיד וְלָא מִיעְצַר, וְאֵינוֹ בָּא עַל יְדֵי תְּפִלַּת הַצַּדִּיקִים.
Nevertheless, dew comes directly from Hashem, may He be blessed, Who bestows it constantly without cessation, and it does not come through the prayers of the righteous.
וְלָזֶה סִידְּרוּ בַּעֲלֵי הַפִּיּוּט הַתְּפִלָּה עַל הַגְּשָׁמִים בְּדֶרֶךְ אָלֶ"ף בֵּי"ת,
Therefore, the composers of the piyutim arranged the prayer for rain in the order of alef-beis,
שֶׁהוּא בָּא עַל יְדֵי מַעֲשֵׂה הַצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁהוּא מִתַּתָּא לְעֵילָּא,
because rain comes through the deeds of the righteous, which is from below to above,
וּמַזְכִּירִין שָׁם זְכוּת אָבוֹת וְהָרוֹעִים שֶׁבִּזְכוּתָם אָנוּ מְבַקְּשִׁים עַל הַגֶּשֶׁם;
and we mention there the merit of the Patriarchs and the shepherds in whose merit we petition for rain;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַתְּפִלָּה עַל הַטַּל סִידְּרוּ בְּדֶרֶךְ תַּשְׁרַ"ק מֵעֵילָּא לְתַתָּא,
whereas the prayer for dew they arranged in the order of tashrak, from above to below,
שֶׁהוּא בָּא מֵה' יִתְבָּרַךְ תָּמִיד דְּלָא מִיעְצַר,
because it comes constantly from Hashem, may He be blessed, and is never withheld
וְסִידְּרוּ: טַל תֵּן וְכוּלֵּי
and so they composed "Dew, grant, etc."
ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מִצִּדּוֹ בְּלֹא מַעֲשֵׂה יְדֵיהֶם שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים, שֶׁה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מַשְׁפִּיעַ הַטַּל תָּמִיד.
from Hashem's own side without the handiwork of the righteous, for Hashem, may He be blessed, bestows dew constantly.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 186a (Tetzaveh) — "Your month is ordered by the sequence of the letters: Aviv, which is Alef-Beis-Gimel — Yud-Beis is the secret of the letter Gimel. But the seventh month, Mine, is from the end of the letters (Tishrei) [Tav-Shin-Reish]. Why? You are from below upward, and I from above downward."

rich.text: Zohar II 186a (Tetzaveh)

— "Your month is ordered by the sequence of the letters: Aviv, which is Alef-Beis-Gimel — Yud-Beis is the secret of the letter Gimel. But the seventh month, Mine, is from the end of the letters (Tishrei) [Tav-Shin-Reish]. Why? You are from below upward, and I from above downward."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Shavuos 7 — “As Tosafos wrote on whether the world was created in Tishrei or Nisan, both are the words of the living God: in Tishrei it arose in thought to be created, and in actuality it was created in Nisan. At first, as it arose in thought to create with the attribute of judgment, it is Tishrei, whose letters run in reverse, indicating judgment; and in the end, after He joined the attribute of mercy, it was created in Nisan, called Aviv, whose letters run in order, Alef-Beis-Gimmel, indicating mercy… Tishrei, with its letters reversed, from above to below, corresponds to the Written Torah, and Nisan is the moon that receives light from the sun, corresponding to the Oral Torah, which receives its light from the Written Torah.” Connection: The same Tosafos and Zohar, adding that Tishrei and Nisan themselves correspond to the Written and Oral Torah.

— “As Tosafos wrote on whether the world was created in Tishrei or Nisan, both are the words of the living God: in Tishrei it arose in thought to be created, and in actuality it was created in Nisan. At first, as it arose in thought to create with the attribute of judgment, it is Tishrei, whose letters run in reverse, indicating judgment; and in the end, after He joined the attribute of mercy, it was created in Nisan, called Aviv, whose letters run in order, Alef-Beis-Gimmel, indicating mercy… Tishrei, with its letters reversed, from above to below, corresponds to the Written Torah, and Nisan is the moon that receives light from the sun, corresponding to the Oral Torah, which receives its light from the Written Torah.” Connection: The same Tosafos and Zohar, adding that Tishrei and Nisan themselves correspond to the Written and Oral Torah.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Likkutei Torah, Shir HaShirim 26 — “It is written, ‘I will be like dew to Israel’—not like rains, which are at times withheld because of the deeds of those below; but dew is never withheld. The reason is that there is an arousal from above that depends on an arousal from below, and there is an arousal from above that does not depend on an arousal from below at all. This is a very lofty level in the Infinite Light, which the arousal from below does not reach. From there the dew descends, and therefore no deed of those below holds it back, nor does any sin or iniquity prevent it, for He acts for His own sake.” Connection: The Alter Rebbe gives the Kabbalistic root of Rav Tzadok's distinction: rain answers the deeds of those below, while dew comes from a level that the deeds of those below do not reach.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Beis Yaakov, Bereishis 2 — “Even permitted speech, such as prayer for bodily needs, is forbidden on Shabbos… as my father, the holy Gaon of Izhbitz, explained: for this reason the Men of the Great Assembly arranged the Musaf prayer in reverse letters, Tav-Shin-Reish-Kuf, because this shows that on Shabbos the letters stand facing the Emanator, while before a person’s eyes they are reversed. That is, on Shabbos a person must see to want only as Hashem’s will is, leave his own understanding, and set up no receiving vessel from his own side.” Connection: The same reading of the reverse alphabet as a flow that comes from God’s side without human effort, applied by the Izhbitzer to the Shabbos Musaf rather than to the prayer for dew.
